correctness.rationale: I independently reconstructed the beta=-3/2 central-charge formulas and BG inequalities. The finite D-gap forces m=1,...,10. Exact enumeration gives 18 oriented records, 9 unordered decompositions and 6 wall loci, with unique outer alpha^2=13/10 represented by two unordered decompositions. The apparent rank restriction 0<=r<=5 is not an assumption: for r>5 the first BG upper bound lies below the alpha-positive threshold, and for r<0 the complementary BG lower bound lies above it, so no outside-rank candidate exists.

originality.broader_coverage: No inspected source gave the exact six-locus census or a stronger classification implying it.
originality.claim_vs_prior_implication: Resultary found only this exact SCOPE record for the 13/10 outer wall. Primary papers on special GM threefold Bridgeland moduli and Serre-invariant stability were inspected; they supply the ambient stability theory and related moduli results but did not state the six-locus census, the 18/9 counts, or the double realization of the outermost locus.
equivalent_formulations: Numerical walls are equality loci of tilt slopes subject to two-factor BG and 0<D(w)<D(v); the outer locus is represented twice by unordered decompositions.

value.rationale: An exhaustive numerical wall census for a natural branch-fixed Kuznetsov class identifies the first potential obstruction and corrects multiplicity of its realization. This is a motivated finite classification useful for subsequent actual-wall analysis, while explicitly distinguishing numerical from geometric walls.
